links.outcome: Agreement of multi-LLM panel fact-checking with human experts in detecting unfaithful summary facts
links.effect: LLM panel vs human panel kappa 0.67 (95% CI 0.61-0.73) at 4/5 LLM agreement; verification scores fell as fact modifications became more severe, showing sensitive error detection.
links.quote: The maximum score for agreement between LLM panel and human experts panel (Cohen’s kappa 0.67 [95% CI, 0.61–0.73]) was observed when a panel of 4 LLMs agreed that the fact was faithful to the original title/abstract, suggesting that acceptance of facts by 4/5 LLMs maximizes agreement with the human panel ( Figure S1A ).

links.outcome: Hallucination rate in LLM-generated scientific summaries of oncology literature
links.effect: Hallucination rate 9.6% (95% CI 6.5-12.7) for INSIDE LLM summaries versus 40.6% (37.8-43.4) for human-written PLS; faithfulness 88.9% vs 61.6%.
links.quote: A higher hallucination rate was identified for human-written PLS than INSIDE summaries (40.6% [95% CI, 37.8–43.4] vs 9.6% [95% CI, 6.5–12.7] for data excluding DeBERTa-v3-base; Table S5 ).

links.outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease) of LLM scientific summaries and plain language summaries
links.effect: INSIDE PLS median FRE 42.3 vs 28.8 for human-written PLS; LLM scientific summaries 24.1, comparable to source abstracts (25.5), i.e., very difficult to read.
links.quote: Importantly, the readability scores for INSIDE PLS were higher compared to the human-written PLS from BioLaySumm (median 42.3 [IQR 35.27–49.41] vs 28.8 [IQR 21.02–36.18]; Figure 4B ).
